articles.headline: New Hall in Philadelphia
articles.summary: The former building used for the Institute for colored youth, on Lombard street, has been remodelled in such a manner that it contains two fine stores on the first floor, having basement rooms under them... On the second floor there is a large hall... The two stores are already occupied, one as a china store kept by Mr. Jeremiah Moore, and the other as a dry goods and trimmings store kept by Mr. Jones. This building is owned by a company of enterprising colored men, being purchased by them at a cost of $10,000. The improvements cost $2,000. There are twelve stock holders, each investing $1,000... among whom we notice Revs. Stephen Smith and Weaver, Messrs. Still, Whipper, Adger and others.

articles.headline: A Want (editorial)
articles.summary: Philadelphians want a Free Reading Room, where young colored men, desiring to pass their leisure moments profitably, may store their minds with information, by reading select works on History, the varied Sciences, Art, and politics, or by engaging in instructive debate. An institution of this character well sustained by the colored people of Philadelphia would add very much to the satisfaction of travellers passing through our city...

articles.headline: Indiana Annual Conference (report by the General Book Steward)
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: Quincy, Ill., Aug. 11th, 1866. Bishop Campbell in the chair... Minutes of the Indiana Conference (non-Philadelphia). Of Philadelphia interest: the Semi-Centenary money ($779.07, committee chaired by Rev. A. McIntosh) was divided in thirds; when Rev. F. Myers moved that one third go to the Book Concern and its property, Bishop Campbell said he would not give one cent until the trustees of the Book Concern told the truth; the reporter wrote that the Bishop had prejudiced the minds of the members against the Book Concern. Rev. Wm. A. Dove recalled first licensing Weaver when he was teaching school at Jeffersonville, Ind.
people: Bishop, chair of the Indiana Conference (printed 'Bishop Campbell')

articles.headline: The Indiana Conference (editorial on Weaver and Bishop Campbell)
articles.summary: In the report of the proceedings of the Indiana Annual Conference, there seems a painful disagreement between the General Book Steward and Bishop Campbell, in reference to the Book Concern. Now we believe that the disagreement is more seeming than real. Bishop Campbell loves the Connection too much 'to prejudice the minds of members of the Conferences' over which he presides, against the Book Concern... He has been in the Book Concern and no one knows more about it than he... our General Book Steward, zealous in the discharge of his duty, in a moment of excitement jotted down in his report what might be misunderstood... Let us try to keep cool.
people: General Book Steward (implied; printed 'our General Book Steward')

articles.headline: Editorial items: Evesham camp meeting; Money Spent on picnics
articles.summary: We learn that Rev. Jacob Mitchel's camp meeting at Eversham, N.J., was very largely attended by all classes of persons. The ministers assisting were Revs. William Moore, Wm. W. Grimes and Theodore Gould. William E. Matthews, agent of the Parent Home and Foreign Missionary Society, was present at the camp and took up a collection amounting to six dollars. There were several converts... Also: 'Money Spent. There has been more money spent for picnics, excursions, &c., by our people in Philadelphia, Baltimore, and Washington this year, than for several previous years; so some who are well posted say.'
people: pastor in charge, Evesham camp meeting (Rev.; printed 'Mitchel', 'Mitchell' Aug 4)

articles.headline: News from A.M.E. Churches: Cape May church freed of debt
articles.summary: Cape May. At last, through the perseverance of Rev. John Cornish and the liberality of strangers, our church at this place is delivered of debt. Brother Cornish had a grand rally a short time since, and sufficient was lifted to pay the entire debt. Thank the Lord!

articles.headline: Aid Society -- Ladies' Aid Society of the A.M.E. Church, Chester
articles.author: E. H. D.
articles.summary: The ladies of the A. M. E. church, of the city of Chester, met on the 20th of June, and organized a Ladies' Aid Society, for the benefit of the Church and ministers. They have accumulated over $50. Up to September 5th, the numbered forty members.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meetings of Chester Circuit
articles.author: Jeremiah Young
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meetings of Chester Circuit will be held as follows: At Hor[?]town, Sept. 29th and 30th, 1866. At Chester, October 6th and 7th. At Chichester, October 13th and 14th. Jeremiah Young, Minister.

articles.headline: Help Wanted -- employment office, 1019 Rodman street (M. A. Williams)
articles.author: M. A. Williams
articles.summary: Wanted immediately--cooks and girls for house work, at the employment office, 1019 Rodman street. M. A. Williams. Sept 15--4t

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Clora Butler, 729 Lisle Street)
articles.author: Clora Butler
articles.summary: Information wanted of my mother and sister. My mother's name was S[?]a Butler, and my sister's name was Louisa [?] Butler. I last heard from them in 1862. They were then in [?] County, Virginia. ... Clora Butler, 729 Lisle Street, Phila., Pa.
people: seeking mother and sister; 729 Lisle Street, Philadelphia

articles.headline: Died (Sep 15 p3): Mrs. Diana Morong; Mrs. Elizabeth Emory; Garrett Evans Simpson
articles.author: James W. Brown
articles.summary: In Philadelphia, Pa., on the morning of the 9th of September, 1866, Mrs. Diana Morong, formerly of Charleston, S.C., in the 83d year of her age. ... Mrs. Elizabeth Emory died August 23d, after a severe illness of four days ... She was born in Cecil, Maryland, in the year 1795. She came to this city at the age of fifteen ... connected herself with Bethel Church, of which she remained a faithful and consistent member till the day of her death. Died, in Camden, N.J., August 11th, 1866, Garrett Evans Simpson, only son of James E. and Sarah J. Simpson, aged 7 weeks and 5 days.
people: deceased Sep 9 1866, formerly of Charleston, S.C., 83d year
deceased Aug 23 1866; b. Cecil Co., Md., 1795; Bethel member

articles.headline: A.M.E. Church news: dedications; Rev. D. P. Seaton; Rev. Wm. Moore at Trenton
articles.summary: Bishop A. W. Wayman will dedicate the A.M.E. Church at Providence, R.I., on the 26th inst. ... The Bishop will also dedicate a church at East Camden, Del., on the 30th inst. Rev. D. P. Seaton raised a collection of two hundred dollars on last Sabbath, to aid in paying off the debt of his church. ... We learn that there are indications of great spiritual prosperity in the charge of Rev. Wm. Moore, at Trenton, N.J.

articles.headline: Correction: James R. Gordon offered the Wesley church suffrage resolutions
articles.summary: Correction.--It was Mr. James R. Gordon who offered the preamble and resolutions at the great suffrage meeting which was held in Wesley church, and not Dr. Kent, as might be understood from incorrect punctuation in our hurried notice of the same in last week's issue of this paper.
people: offered preamble and resolutions, Wesley church suffrage meeting (Mr.)

articles.headline: Great Union Fair (to aid the Book Concern)
articles.summary: A great Union Fair will be held to aid the Book Concern. More about it next week.

articles.headline: Personal Items (Sep 22)
articles.summary: Bishop A. W. Wayman has recovered ... Revs. Jonathan Hamilton and D. P. Seaton went to Baltimore this week, where they intend to spend the Sabbath. Rev. E. Weaver will deliver a special discourse on Sabbath evening, the 23d inst., in Bethel Church, on the 'Existence of God.'

articles.headline: Our Book Concern (letter)
articles.author: Henry McNeal Turner
articles.summary: Philadelphia, August 29th, 1866. Mr. Editor:--The General Book Committee has had a standing notice in the Christian Recorder for over two months, calling upon the ministers of the A. M. E. Church to support the Book Concern. I have read this notice with shame and regret.

articles.headline: Home for Aged and Infirm Colored People -- An Appeal
articles.summary: Although aid is often solicited by benevolent institutions, and in view of the fact that many of our citizens have been unusually successful in business during the past few years, it is hoped that an appeal at this time, on behalf of the 'Home for Aged and Infirm Colored Persons,' 340 South Front Street, Philadelphia, will not be in vain.
people: Chairman, Board of Managers, 632 Powell Street (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notice: M. W. Grand Lodge for the State of Pennsylvania, A. Y. M. -- new lodges in Petersburg, Va.
articles.author: Daniel Johnson
articles.summary: A. L. 5866. Philadelphia, September 10th, A. D. 1866. M. W. Grand Lodge for the State of Pennsylvania, A. Y. M., South Seventh Street. To proclaim and encourage virtue, in whatever form it appears, is truly laudable ... The Grand Master, Brother Jonathan Miller, has established three Lodges in Petersburg, Va.
people: Grand Master, M. W. Grand Lodge of Pennsylvania (Brother)

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly meetings, Burlington, Mount Holly and Evesham, N.J.
articles.author: Jacob Mitchell
articles.summary: Quarterly Meeting Conference will take place at Burlington, N.J., October 13th, 1866, at ten o'clock, A.M.; the pastor requests all the members to be present. Quarterly Meeting at Mount Holly, October 21st, 1866. Quarterly Meeting at Evesham, October 28th, 1866. Jacob Mitchell, Pastor.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Henry Collins; Johanna Williams)
articles.summary: Any one who may chance to know any thing concerning the whereabouts of Henry Collins, will please inform his brother, James Collins, who is residing in Princeton, N.J. The said Henry was formerly owned by Mrs Sarah Harris, of Queen Ann County, Md. ... Information wanted of the whereabouts of my daughter, Johanna Williams. I last seen her in January, 1866. ... Charlotte A. Williams, at Chester City, Delaware Co., Pa.
people: seeking brother; residing in Princeton, N.J.
sought; formerly enslaved in Queen Ann County, Md.
seeking daughter; Chester City, Delaware Co., Pa.

articles.headline: Lodgings -- 410 Gaskill Street
articles.summary: A few gentlemen can obtain lodging by applying at 410 [G]askill Street, Philadelphia. Sept. 22--1t.

articles.headline: Died: George Bedford, son of Mary Bedford of Philadelphia
articles.summary: On the 2d ult., in New York City, George Bedford, son of Mary Bedford, of Philadelphia.

articles.headline: J. H. Moore's China, Glass, and Queensware Store, No. 706 Lombard Street (advertisement)
articles.summary: J. H. Moore's China, Glass, and Queensware Store, No. 706 Lombard Street, (Under Liberty Hall,) Philadelphia. Orders received for Coal. Sept. 22--3mo.
people: proprietor, china, glass and queensware store, No. 706 Lombard Street (under Liberty Hall)

articles.headline: Reply of the Corresponding Secretary to 'Has Our Church a Missionary Society?'
articles.author: John M. Brown
articles.summary: Xenia, Sept. 11th, 1866. Reply to Brother S. [T. G. Steward]'s letter: explains the Parent Home and Foreign Missionary Society's accounts and remittances. 'The Philadelphia Conference, having no Southern work, sent all of its Semi-Centenary money ($611 50) to the Treasurer of the P. H. and F. Missionary Society, but retained all of its other missionary money in the hands of the local Treasurer.'

articles.headline: South Carolina Correspondence (R. H. Cain): Wm. M. Johnson, T. G. Steward, A. L. Stanford
articles.author: R. H. Cain
articles.summary: Charleston, S.C., Sept. 18th, 1866. Report on the South Carolina mission: ... appointed Brother Wm. M. Johnson, formerly of Philadelphia, as pastor ... Brother T. G. Steward has arrived and has charge of the Morris Street church [Charleston] ... Brother A. L. Stanford is moving forward in Georgia.
people: formerly of Philadelphia; appointed pastor in South Carolina (Brother)
arrived in Charleston; in charge of Morris Street church

articles.headline: Our Banner to the Breeze in Washington (Miss Sallie Daffin, of Philadelphia)
articles.author: W. E. M.
articles.summary: Washington, D.C. letter on the A.M.E. churches of Washington and Baltimore in 'this Semi-Centenary year': Israel Church (Rev. Wm. H. Hunter) has opened a day school for females in its basement; Miss Sallie Daffin, of Philadelphia, has charge of the school.
people: teacher in charge of Israel Church female day school, Washington; of Philadelphia (Miss)

articles.headline: Philadelphia a Paradox (editorial)
articles.summary: In no city of the Union are a more liberty-loving people found than in this city ... Yet while it is a fact that there is such a strong liberty-loving spirit among the whites ... Philadelphia is more unmerciful in her proscription of colored men than any other city in the Union. The street cars, public places of amusement and instruction, and the passenger rooms at the depots, prove the truth of this assertion.

articles.headline: Our Missionaries Going South (Revs. Charles Pearce and C. L. Bradwell)
articles.summary: Revs. Charles Pearce and C. L. Bradwell, of the South Carolina Conference, left New York for Savannah this week; Bro. Pearce, with his family, en route to Tallahassee, Florida; Bro. Bradwell to Edisto Island.

articles.headline: The Great Union Fair for the Book Concern
articles.summary: This Fair will take place in a few weeks. All of the A. M. E. churches in this city have united to get it up; and so it is expected that the congregations thereof will be specially interested in it ... Rev. Elisha Weaver, the General Book Steward, has made an appeal to the citizens of Philadelphia (by and with the approval of his committee) for aid to meet current expenses and the debts on the newly purchased property.

articles.headline: Editorial items: E. D. Bassett; Institute for Colored Youth examinations
articles.summary: E. D. Bassett.--Few colored men are doing more for their race than E. D. Bassett, the Principal of the Institute for colored youth. He is thorough in all that he does ... The educated gentlemen who control the institution know full well his worth, and have favored him with many recognitions of it, the most important of which is the very liberal support in the way of salary and residence which they give him. ... Preparing for Examination.--They are as busy as bees at the Institute for colored youth, in this city, preparing for examination.

articles.headline: A.M.E. Church Items: Zion Mission meetings; Macedonia, Camden; West Philadelphia Circuit
articles.summary: A highly interesting series of meetings are being held at Zion Mission A. M. E. church, Rev. T. Gould, Pastor. These meetings are held day and night, and have been in progress about two weeks. Several persons have professed religion. ... Macedonia church, Camden, N.J., Rev. Geo. Boyer, Pastor, is in a highly prosperous condition. ... We learn that the West Philadelphia Circuit, under the charge of Rev. Henry J. Rhodes, is enjoying great spiritual progress.
people: in charge of West Philadelphia Circuit (Rev.)

articles.headline: Centenary of Methodism -- To the Ministers and Members of the Philadelphia District
articles.author: James Lynch, Secretary
articles.summary: We, the undersigned Centenary Committee, in pursuance of the recommendation of the presiding Bishop and his colleagues, beg leave to earnestly remind you that you are to celebrate, in common with the great Methodist family of the United States, the one hundredth year of the existence of Methodism on this continent.

articles.headline: Religious Items: Rev. F. T. Boas at the colored Baptist church, West Philadelphia
articles.summary: Rev. F. T. Boas, a very youthful divine, formerly of the Joy St. Baptist church, Boston, is laboring very acceptably at the colored Baptist church, West Philadelphia. A demonstration to aid this church will take place October 2d.
people: pastor, colored Baptist church, West Philadelphia (Rev.)

articles.headline: Going South: Mr. Richard Gleaves
articles.summary: Going South.--Mr. Richard Gleaves, of this city, will sail for Beaufort, S. C., in a few days. He will go into business at that place. Mr. Gleaves is one of our most valued citizens, and it is with deep regret that we see him leave our city.
people: of Philadelphia; leaving for Beaufort, S.C. to go into business (Mr.)

articles.headline: 'It is Invaluable' -- Macamoose Tonic prepared by Rev. I. R. Gates
articles.summary: We do not generally recommend medicines in our editorial columns, but having lately used the 'Macamoose Tonic,' prepared by Rev. I. R. Gates, and found it such a great remedy for Bronchitis and sore throat ... For sale at 1230 Wood St. and 1618 North 11th. Try it ... 2t.
people: preparer of 'Macamoose Tonic' (Rev.); sold at 1230 Wood St. and 1618 North 11th

articles.headline: Notice: Rev. James Lynch to preach at the M. E. church, Fourth Street
articles.summary: Rev. James Lynch will preach in the M. E. church, Fourth street, between Market and Arch, (Rev. Mr. Carrow's,) to-morrow (Sunday) evening, at half-past 7 o'clock.

articles.headline: Special Notice: Grand Fair in Liberty Hall for the Book Concern and Christian Recorder
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: To the Ministers of the Philadelphia and New York Annual Conferences. Dear Brethren: I wish to call your attention to the grand Fair to be held in the Liberty Hall, Lombard street, Philadelphia, Pa., by the Book Committee, for the benefit of the Book Concern and Christian Recorder. The Fair will open on Thursday, November 1st, 1866, and continue two weeks.

articles.headline: Notice: Grand Union Centenary Meeting at the A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street
articles.author: William M. Watson, Pastor
articles.summary: A Grand Union Centenary Meeting will be held all day, on Sunday, the 30th inst., in the A. M. E. Wesley church, Hurst Street. This being the hundredth year of Methodism in America, and the fiftieth year of the existence of our Church, we deem it but proper that we assemble in remembrance of this eventful period in our history.

articles.headline: Equal Rights Demonstration at the Oak Street Baptist Church, West Philadelphia
articles.summary: A demonstration, in favor of equal rights, will take place at the Oak Street Baptist Church, West Philadelphia, on Tuesday evening, October 2d, 1866, consisting of the following array of eminent speakers ... Revs. T. D. Miller, C. Leonard, F. T. Boas, and a host of others. ... After the speeches a grand oyster feast will be given; proceeds to be used for the reparation of the church.

articles.headline: A Fair at the Masonic Hall for Zion Baptist Church of Kaighnsville, N.J.
articles.summary: A fair for the sale of useful and fancy articles, will be held in the Masonic Hall, Eleventh St., below Pine, commencing Monday, Oct. 1st, 1866, and continue during the week, for the benefit of Zion Baptist Church, of Keighnsville, N. J.

articles.headline: Quarterly meeting notices: Salem Station; Zion Mission; Frankford
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meeting of Salem Station will take place on the 7th of October ... N. H. Turpin, Minister in Charge. Quarterly Meeting of Zion Mission A. M. E. church, will be held on Sabbath, the 14th day of October, 1866 ... T. Gould, Minister in Charge. The Quarterly Meeting, at Frankford, Pa., will be held on the first Sabbath in October. ... J. H. Smith, Elder.
people: minister in charge, Zion Mission A.M.E. church

articles.headline: To the People of Color -- lessons in French, English and Spanish (C. A. M[?], 804 Lombard St.)
articles.summary: The undersigned begs leave to inform the public that she will be prepared to give lessons in the French, English and Spanish languages, on the 1st of October next, and hopes by her proficiency in the several branches, to merit a share of their patronage. Terms, moderate. Please apply to C. A. M[?], 804 Lombard St. above 8th. Aug. 29[sic]--1t.

articles.headline: Resolutions on the death of Alexander Bascome
articles.author: J. D. Cooper; J. S. Price; Wm. C. Boliver
articles.summary: The following preamble and resolutions on the demise of the late Alexander Bascome, were unanimously approved. Whereas, it has pleased an all-wise Providence ... to remove from the scene of his earthly labors in a distant State, our late fellow member, Alexander Bascome ...
people: deceased member (died in a distant State)

articles.headline: Information Wanted: Daniel Nelson (by Frank Nelson, 420 South 7th Street)
articles.author: Frank Nelson
articles.summary: Information wanted of my brother Daniel Nelson. The last time I saw him, he was in Nelson, Prince George County, Md., in 1861. Any information of his whereabouts will be thankfully received by his brother, Frank Nelson, 420 South 7th Street, Philadelphia, Pa. Ministers please notice. Sept. 29--1t.
people: sought; last seen Prince George County, Md., 1861

articles.headline: Wanted: apprentices, 401 South Seventh Street
articles.summary: Two or three apprentices wanted. None but good sewers need apply at 401 South Seventh Street. Sept. 29--4t.

events.name: Sunday School Picnic of the Central Presbyterian and Shiloh Baptist churches (and melee)
events.location: Diamond Cottage (grounds outside the city, reached from Philadelphia)
events.description: Annual picnic of the Sunday schools of the Central Presbyterian and Shiloh Baptist churches, Monday July 2, 1866: left Philadelphia about 9 o'clock, arrived at Diamond Cottage about ten; some 200 scholars of each school in procession; about 4000 persons on the ground. After the children left, a man refused to pay the innkeeper and was arrested by police; friends rescued him; fire bells were rung and a melee followed with arrests. Mr. Isaiah White, son of Mr. Jacob C. White Sr., was seriously injured though not connected with the affair; a son of Mr. Francis was badly beaten. (Processions/parades and police-violence topics.)

events.name: Celebration of the Fourth of July by Colored Citizens, Masonic Hall
events.description: Large meeting of colored citizens at Masonic Hall on the Fourth of July; speeches by Messrs. Bowers, [Lancoot? VERIFY] and others; resolutions pledging devotion to the country and zeal to procure equal rights. Same issue: Mrs. F. E. W. Harper spoke at the Freedmen's Fair on the evening of the Fourth. Speakers printed by surname only: not linked.

events.name: Bristol Circuit quarterly meetings (Bristol, Bensalem, and a third appointment)
events.description: First quarterly meeting at Bristol July 7-8 (quarterly conference Sat. July 7, 3 PM; love feast Sunday 9:30); Bensalem July 14-15; a third appointment July 21-22 (place name unclear). Signed Thomas M. Kinnard, Minister in Charge, July 6, 1866 (the second Bristol notice prints 'Kennard').
attendees: minister in charge, Bristol circuit (printed also 'Kennard')

events.name: West Philadelphia Circuit quarterly meetings (Norristown, Germantown, West Philadelphia)
events.description: Quarterly meeting of the A.M.E. Church, West Philadelphia Circuit: Norristown, Pa., Sunday July 15, 1866 (love feast 9 AM); Germantown, conference Saturday 2 PM, meeting July 22; West Philadelphia July 29, 1866. Signed H. J. Rhodes, June 30.

events.name: Burlington Circuit quarterly meetings
events.location: Evesham, Mount Holly and Burlington, N.J.
events.description: Quarterly meetings of Burlington Circuit: Evesham July 8; Mount Holly July 15; Burlington July 22. Jacob Mitchell, minister in charge.

events.name: Princeton Circuit quarterly conference and meetings
events.location: Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church, Witherspoon Street, Princeton, N.J.; Union church, Rocky Hill
events.description: Quarterly conference Princeton Circuit July 14 at Mount Pisgah church, Witherspoon Street; quarterly meeting 15th; the 22d at Union church, Rocky Hill; the 29th at a third place (name unclear). J. B. Hamilton, Minister.

events.name: Woodbury / Dutchtown / Cashtown quarterly meetings
events.description: Quarterly meeting at Woodbury Sunday 22d inst.; Rev. N. H. Turpin at Dutchtown Sunday 29th; Cashtown first Sunday in August. Wm. W. Grimes, Elder.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church (Coates Street) quarterly meeting
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly meeting Sunday July 15, 1866: 10 1/2 AM Rev. James Lynch; 3 PM Rev. Joseph H. Smith; 8 PM Rev. E. Weaver. R. P. Gibbs, Pastor.

events.name: Bordentown Circuit quarterly conference and meetings
events.description: Quarterly conference of Bordentown Circuit Saturday July 7, 1 1/2 PM; quarterly meeting at Allentown 14-15; Cookstown 22d. Signed Peter Gardiner, preacher in charge, June 23.

events.name: Quarterly meeting at Wesley Church, Hurst Street (Little Wesley)
events.description: Quarterly meeting at Wesley Church, Hurst Street (Little Wesley, A.M.E.), Sunday 15th inst.: 10 AM Rev. Wm. Watson; 3 PM Rev. James Lynch; 8 PM Rev. Joseph Smith. Wm. Watson, Pastor.

events.name: Freedmen's Fair (continuing), Fourth of July evening
events.description: The Freedmen's Fair, managed by ladies and displaying the flags of the colored regiments, continued over the Fourth; on the evening of the Fourth Mrs. F. E. W. Harper gave a short speech; the fair to close Tuesday next. (Continuation of the fair captured last quarter.)

events.name: Grand Lecture by Mrs. F. E. W. Harper, Union A.M.E. Church
events.location: A.M.E. Union church, Coates street below Fifth, Philadelphia
events.description: Lecture 'United We Stand--Divided We Fall', subject 'The Colored Man as a Social and Political Force', by Mrs. F. E. W. Harper, Tuesday evening July 17, 1866. A Committee of Ladies to keep a refreshment table in the basement. Tickets 25 cents at the A.M.E. Book Store, Pine street below Seventh. Committee of Arrangements: Wm. Thos. Simpson, John Lee Clower [VERIFY; p2 editorial prints 'Glover'], William H. Davis and Rev. R. P. Gibbs.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League -- annual meeting called (Pittsburgh)
events.description: Call issued at Philadelphia July 7 by order of the Executive Board for the annual meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League at Pittsburgh, August 8, 1866, 10 AM; societies not represented urged to join and send representatives; auxiliaries to send annual reports to the Recording Secretary. Signed Wm. Nesbit, President; J. C. White, Jr. and C. B. Colly [VERIFY], Secretaries. A second notice (July 12) by J. C. White, Jr., Recording Secretary: excursion tickets on the Pennsylvania Railroad, full fare going, return free. Wm. Nesbit (League president; not a Philadelphian) is named in text only.

events.name: New Hall on Lombard Street (former Institute for Colored Youth building) -- purchase by stock company
events.description: The former ICY building on Lombard street remodelled: two stores on the first floor with basement rooms, a large hall on the second floor; proposed 40-foot rear extension. Stores occupied by Mr. Jeremiah Moore [VERIFY] (china) and Mr. Jones (dry goods and trimmings; = Mr. A. P. Jones of the same page). Owned by a company of colored men: bought for $10,000, improvements $2,000; twelve stockholders at $1,000 each, among them Revs. Stephen Smith and Weaver, Messrs. Still, Whipper, Adger and others. (Same hall as the Freedmen's Fair hall captured last quarter.)

events.name: Bethel Church Sabbath School gift to A.M.E. missionaries in the Mississippi Valley
events.description: Bishop J. P. Campbell (Richmond, Ind., July 6, 1866) acknowledges $50 from the Executive Board of Bethel church Sabbath School, Sixth street, Philadelphia, for the relief of missionaries in the Mississippi Valley, plus $1 each from Rev. Mr. Cookman, Rev. Mr. Menship [?], Dr. Armstrong, $1 from faithful members of Bethel church and 50 cts from another member: total $54.50. Funds to be sent to his address at No. 1?10 Addison street, Philadelphia [VERIFY number], or to Rev. John Turner (New Orleans), Rev. J. W. Early (Louisville) or Rev. A. T. Hall (Chicago). (Southern missions / migrations topic.)

events.name: Freehold Station quarterly meeting
events.description: Quarterly Meeting of Freehold Station July 14 and 15, 1866; members requested to fast; love-feast 9 AM. Wm. H. Turner, Minister in Charge.

events.name: A.M.E. church at Reading -- bush-meeting
events.description: The A.M.E. church at Reading will hold a bush-meeting commencing August 11 and continuing over Sabbath; Revs. J. Lynch, J. Mitchell and others to be present. T. A. Cuff, Minister in Charge. (Camp meeting season.)

events.name: Union Semi-Centenary Camp Meeting, Bristol Circuit
events.location: Edenton [sic; prob. Eddington] Station, Bristol Circuit, in Charles Vandergraph's [VERIFY] Woods
events.description: A.M.E. SEMI-CENTENARY topic (record separately for the owner). Union Semi-Centenary camp meeting at 'Edenton' Station, Bristol Circuit, commencing August 3 and to continue until 'the 6th of September' (as printed); proceeds to liquidate the debt on the Bristol Church; '150,000 persons' expected from all parts of the United States and the Canadas; fare from Philadelphia 25 cts. Signed Thomas M. Kinnard, Elder in charge of Bristol Circuit.

events.name: Union camp meeting near the Evesham church (N.J.)
events.location: Samuel Evans' woods, near the Evesham church, N.J.
events.description: Union camp meeting commencing the third Friday in August 1866 (Aug. 17), for the benefit of the new church at Evesham; no selling within two miles; Bishop Wayman, Revs. W. W. Grimes, M. F. Sluby, James Lynch and others expected; Evesham stage from Arch Street Ferry, Camden. Committee of Arrangements (names partly uncertain): William Mass[?], John Thompson, Jefferson Johnson, Charles Green, William Roberts, Jos. Winder, Stephen Johnson, Charles Lopemmine[?], Robert Davis. Jacob M. Mitchell, Pastor. (Committee names given in text only: common or uncertain names, Burlington circuit, NJ.) (Notice reprinted Aug 4, 1866, which adds the committee of arrangements: William Muse, Jefferson Johnson, Charles Green, William Roberts, Stephen Johnson, Robert Davis.)

events.name: Lecture by Mrs. F. E. W. Harper at Wesley church, Lombard Street (Big Wesley)
events.location: Wesley church, Lombard Street below 6th, Philadelphia
events.description: Mrs. F. E. W. Harper to lecture Wednesday evening July 25, 1866, at 8 1/2 o'clock, on 'The colored man a social and political force'; tickets 20 cents. Printed 'Wesley church, Lombard Street' = BIG WESLEY (A.M.E. Zion) under the owner's ruling. Repeat of her Union church lecture of July 17.

events.name: Banneker Institute -- Fourth of July resolutions
events.description: Resolutions passed by the Banneker Institute on the Fourth of July 1866: demanding impartial suffrage, praising the majority in Congress and criticising the Constitutional Amendment. Members named only by surname in the item (White, Adger, Catto, Lacount and others): not linked.

events.name: McCrummell Equal Rights League of Bensalem -- public-school admission won
events.description: Report from Miss Sarah L. Purvis, Corresponding Secretary: the McCrummell Equal Rights League of Bensalem drew up a petition and appointed a committee to wait on the school Directors; after discussion the colored children received full permission to attend any of the public schools in the district. Signed 'P.'

events.name: Book Committee called meeting
events.description: Called meeting of the A.M.E. Book Committee, Monday July 23, 1866. E. Weaver, Chairman; James Lynch, Secretary.

events.name: Arrival of Rev. Theophilus Steward from South Carolina; Rev. Charles L. Bradwell from Savannah
events.description: MIGRATIONS / southern missions: Rev. Theophilus Steward and his wife arrived in Philadelphia from South Carolina (Personal Items, p3); Rev. Charles L. Bradwell of Savannah, Ga., A.M.E. elder, arrived in the city July 16 soliciting aid for a church on Edisto Island (p2). Rev. A. L. Stanford (the Recorder's Philadelphia corresponding editor) reported prospering at Savannah and expected in Philadelphia soon (p2). Rev. T. M. D. Ward of California expects to come East in 1867 (p2).

events.name: First Grand Pic-Nic of the Equal Rights League at Reading, with the Delany Guards
events.description: PROCESSIONS/excursions and Equal Rights League topics. First Grand Pic-Nic of the Equal Rights League at Reading, August 1, 1866 (West India Emancipation day); speakers Mr. Wm. Nesbit, President of the State League, and others; excursion tickets on the Philadelphia & Reading Railroad and all its branches at half-fare; the 'Delany Guards' of Harrisburg (colored military company, read from the image; no officers named) to attend; Mrs. Frances Ellen Watkins Harper to lecture in the evening.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League -- annual meeting call (Wylie Street Church, Pittsburgh)
events.location: Wylie Street Church, Pittsburgh; issued from the Bureau of the League, 717 Lombard Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Address 'To the Colored People of Pennsylvania', dated Bureau of Pa. State Equal Rights' League, 717 Lombard Street, Philadelphia, July 16, 1866: annual meeting at the Wylie Street Church, Pittsburgh, Wednesday August 8, 10 AM; auxiliary leagues to send delegates; localities without leagues to form them; demand for 'Justice and enfranchisement without regard to race or color'; appeal to the memory of colored soldiers; return passes free over the Philadelphia & Erie R.R. and Pennsylvania Central and branches, good until August 15. Signed by order of the Board: William Nesbit, Pres't; Jacob C. White, Jr., Charles B. Colly [VERIFY], Secretaries. Note the League's Philadelphia bureau address, 717 Lombard Street.

events.name: Macedonia A.M.E. Sabbath School (Camden, N.J.) excursion to Red Bank
events.description: Excursion of the A.M.E. Macedonia Sabbath School of Camden, N.J., to Red Bank, August 8, 1866; adults 40 cts, children 20 cts; tickets from the committee and at the Recorder office. Committee of Arrangements: D. G. Harris, O. L. Davis, R. M. Barnes. Same page: grand jubilee of Macedonia church (debt paid) on the first Sunday in August (Aug. 5), Rev. G. E. Boyer [VERIFY] in charge; D. G. Harris, Secretary. (Notice reprinted Aug 4, 1866.)

events.name: Harvest Home and Festival, Mt. Zion A.M.E. church, Trenton
events.location: Evans' woods, Princeton turnpike, about 1 1/2 miles from Trenton, N.J.; church in the evening
events.description: Harvest Home and Festival held by the ladies of Trenton, N.J., Thursday August 2, 1866; speakers on the ground and at the church (Mt. Zion A.M.E.) in the evening. William Moore, Pastor. (Identity of this William Moore of Trenton vs. Rev. William Moore of Bethel 1864-66 is an open owner question: recorded as printed.)
attendees: pastor, Mt. Zion A.M.E., Trenton [identity vs. Bethel's Rev. William Moore open]

events.name: Downingtown quarterly conference; New Centreville camp meeting; Mount Zion (Chester Co.) bush meeting
events.location: Downingtown; New Centreville; Mount Zion A.M.E. church, Penningtonville [VERIFY], Chester county
events.description: Downingtown quarterly conference held 'last Saturday' (July 21), the ladies providing supper, address by Rev. W. R. Norris; camp meeting at New Centreville Aug 30 - Sept 5 by Rev. Wm. R. Norris and Edward Lawe (minister in charge). Bush and quarterly meeting at Mount Zion A.M.E. church, Chester county, from Saturday August 4, quarterly conference 1 o'clock; Wm. R. Norris, Minister in Charge.

events.name: Death of Mrs. Sarah Bacon on her way to the Bethel love-feast
events.location: opposite the hospital, near Bethel Church, corner Sixth and Lombard Sts., Philadelphia
events.description: Monday evening (July 23, 1866) Mrs. Sarah Bacon [VERIFY], aged 52, member of Bethel thirty years and niece of the late Mrs. Elizabeth Harris, collapsed and died while walking to the love-feast at Bethel Church. The love-feast was presided over by Rev. James Hollen, pastor (p2, A.M.E. Church Items).

events.name: Camp meeting at Milford, New Jersey (Rev. Andrew Till)
events.location: Milford, New Jersey; cars from Vine Street Landing to Long-a-Coming
events.description: A camp meeting will be held at Milford, New Jersey, by Rev. Andrew Till, commencing August 25th. Persons desirous of attending will take the cars at Vine Street Landing, which will convey them to Long-a-Coming, about three miles from the grounds, where means of conveyance to the ground will be in waiting. Ministers will be warmly welcomed and well provided for. Aug 4-1t.

events.name: Centenary Sabbath School walk and harvest home of the Union Sabbath School of the A.M.E. Bethel Church of Frankford
events.location: Large's woods, one mile from Frankford
events.description: The Union Sabbath School of the A.M.E. Bethel Church of Frankford intend having a centenary Sabbath School walk and harvest home on the 17th of August, 1866, in Large's woods, one mile from Frankford, for the benefit of Rev. Joseph H. Smith. Rev. J. R. V. Morgan will deliver an address at 3 o'clock. Several eminent speakers will address the school. 'Hear the cry of little Bethel, and come out and help us.' Signed Joseph H. Smith, Elder; Joseph G. Fay [VERIFY], Superintendent. In case of stormy weather, the school will go the next Monday. aug 12-2t. (Parades/processions topic: Sabbath-school walk. 'Centenary' as printed -- probably the Centenary of Methodism year; do not merge with the A.M.E. Semi-Centenary.)

events.name: Grand Fruit Festival of the Shaba [VERIFY] Lodge No. 1, Juvenile Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria
events.location: Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street below Pine, Philadelphia
events.description: A Grand Fruit Festival of the Shaba [VERIFY: Shaba/Sheba] Lodge, No. 1, of Juvenile Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria, will be held in the city of Philadelphia, at the Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street, below Pine, on Monday evening, August 20th, at which time there will be addresses delivered by John R. Porter, Grand Chief of the State of New York, John R. V. Morgan [VERIFY final letters], of Philadelphia, and M. B. Cass [VERIFY], past Grand Chief of New York. The committee will spare no pains... Guardians: A. Cropper and S. Young. Secretary: Caroline Stokes. aug 12th-2t. (Society meeting; Porter and Cass are New York, text only.)

events.name: Camp meeting at Media, Delaware Co., Pa., for the new A.M.E. Church at Media
events.description: A united camp meeting will be held at Media, Delaware Co., Pa., for the benefit of the new A.M.E. Church at Media, commencing on the 22d of August, and to be continued to the 29th. General invitation to all churches... arrangements with the superintendent of the West Chester Railroad Company to sell excursion tickets and to carry all ministers employed free of charge. Persons wishing a stand or boarding tent apply to the committee at Media. Committee: William Dobson, Aaron Moman [VERIFY], George Boston, Joshua Blakes, Benj. Brown, and others. Yours in Christ, Jas. V. Pierce, Minister in Charge. Aug. 11-2t.

events.name: Harvest Home at Princeton, N.J.
events.description: A Harvest Home will be held at Princeton, N.J., on Wednesday the 22d inst. Mrs. Frances E. W. Harper, Revs. D. P. Seaton, Theo. Gould, and Wm. Moore, will deliver addresses. A hearty invitation is extended to the public... Should the weather prove unfavorable the meeting will take place on the 23d. Jonathan B. Hamilton, Minister in charge.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, annual meeting at Pittsburgh
events.description: Proceedings of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League at the annual meeting held in the city of Pittsburgh, August 8, 9, 10, 1866. President [William] Nesbit in the chair; J. C. White, Jr., and O. V. Catto, secretaries; prayer by Rev. Jos. A. Nelson of Philadelphia. PHILADELPHIA CITY delegates: Rev. Joseph A. Nelson, Octavius V. Catto, Joseph C. Bustill, Jacob C. White, Jr., Wm. D. Forten, David B. Bowser, George B. White, Lewis N. Bedford, Robert M. Adger, Alfred M. Green, J. McC. Crummill. Honorary member listed for Philadelphia: J. M. White (also 'M. E. Wolf[?]'). Other delegates (text only): Allegheny Co.: Rev. John Peck, Prof. Geo. B. Vashon, Benj. F. Pulpress, H. R. Williamson, Thomas Roach[?], G. W. Itimey[?]; Bedford: William T. Burke; Berks: Aaron L. Still, Reading (Unity E.R. League); Blair: John Alexander, Thomas R. Shorter, William Nesbit, Altoona, Daniel Williams, Hollidaysburg; Bradford: Solomon Cooper; BUCKS: Wm. B. Purvis, Bensalem; William A. Burley[?], Bristol; George W. Bush[?], Attleboro'; Lewis Hartless, Buckingham; Cambria: Samuel C. Johnson; Centre: John Welch; CHESTER: Jonathan Betts, Oxford; Cumberland: George H. Jenkins, And. G. Washington, Levi Lee, G. Barnes; Dauphin: O. L. C. Hughes, George W. Saunders, Cassius M. Brown, Rev. John E. Price, Rev. C. J. Carter, Charles H. Vance; Fayette: Benj. W. Arnett, Brownsville; Franklin: Moses Anderson, James Lewis; Huntingdon: John G. Chaplin, James H. Gant; Indiana: David Brown; Lawrence: Chas. W. Nighten, Lemuel B. Stewart; Lycoming: Enoch Gilchrist, Rev. John H. Spriggs; Northampton: Wm. E. Walch. Business: J. C. Bustill moved suspension of rules; resolution of D. Williams that no one be elected who had opposed the State League, opposed by A. M. Green; press committee on Green's motion (Vashon, Pulpress, C. J. Carter); credentials committee on Catto's motion: Joseph C. Bustill, Daniel Williams, Aaron L. Still, Enoch Gilchrist, Thomas R. Shorter; credentials received from the Lincoln E. R. League, Philadelphia (Lewis N. Bedford, printed 'Bredford'); Bowser moved a business committee (one per county; Philadelphia: William D. Forten); A. M. Green secretary pro tem and assistant secretary with Cassius M. Brown; Rev. Jos. A. Nelson chaplain; nominating committee (Philadelphia: George B. White, whose appointment Catto moved to reconsider, saying R. M. Adger was not a member; lost); president's annual message referred to D. Williams, D. B. Bowser, O. V. Catto; W. D. Forten raised the standing of C. H. Vance of Harrisburg, Bustill contending he was not a member; chair ruled for Vance, sustained on Catto's appeal 24 to 20; on motion of J. McC. Crummill a committee (Crummill, D. B. Bowser, B. F. Pulpress) to invite Hon. John W. Forney, Ex-Gov. Hamilton of Texas, Hon. T. J. Bingham, Hon. Thos. Williams and Senator J. S. Graham. Revs. J. J. Clinton and J. W. Loguen invited to speak. Report to be continued; the Pittsburgh letter (same page) says the League adjourned sine die on the third day and next meets at Reading.
attendees: delegate, Philadelphia; secretary (printed 'Jacob C. White, Jr.' and 'J. C. White, Jr.')

events.name: National Equal Rights League -- call for annual meeting at Nashville
events.location: Nashville, Tenn. (call issued from the League's rooms, Philadelphia)
events.description: Call dated at the Rooms of the National Equal Rights League, Philadelphia, Pa., Aug. [day illegible] 1866, signed by order John M. Langston, Pres't. Recalls the annual meeting at Cleveland, Ohio, Oct. 19-21, 1865, which fixed the next annual meeting at Nashville, Tenn., 10 A.M., 18 September 1866, for election of officers and other business; invites members, representatives of auxiliary associations and subordinate leagues, and friends. Object: complete equality before the law; asks where colored Americans stand legally and politically since the rebellion; representation: one representative for each $5 contributed annually by an auxiliary or subordinate league and one for each further $3; hopes for a grand national gathering on Southern soil. No officers other than Langston and no delegates are named in this printing (Langston is Ohio: text only). NOTE: the brief's 'Annual Meeting' item is this CALL; the meeting itself had not yet happened.

events.name: A.M.E. Semi-Centenary Camp Meeting, Bristol Circuit, in Mr. Chas. Vandergrift's woods
events.location: Mr. Chas. Vandergrift's Woods near Edgington [VERIFY] Station, Pa., 1 1/4 miles from the station (Bristol Circuit)
events.description: There will be a Semi-Centenary Camp Meeting of the A.M.E. Church, on Bristol Circuit, commencing on the 23d of August and closing on the 5th [VERIFY] of September, 1866. Reached from Philadelphia by the Steamboat Pilot Boy, leaving Arch street wharf at 7 A.M. and 2 P.M., returning 1 P.M. and 5 P.M. (Sundays 9 A.M. and 2 P.M.), stopping at Beckley's Landing; excursion tickets 40 cents; also by railroad from the Kensington Depot (reached by the Third and Fifth street cars), stopping at Andalusia Station. 'This being the Fiftieth year of the existence of the A.M.E. Church, we therefore intend to celebrate the same on this occasion'; invites all bishops, ministers and members in the United States and Canada; expects at least 150,000 persons. A sermon on the Emancipation of our Brethren in the South. Rules: no spirituous liquors within two miles; no stands within one mile unless permitted; boarding tents, meat and bread stands, feed stand. Committee: George Longstreth, James Tilman, Henry Blake, William Chase, Joseph Morgan, Edward Jenkins, Charles Anderson, Joseph Ross, Peter Watson, Joseph Limehouse, John Williams, Andrew Ricketts. Thos. M. Kinnaird, Minister in Charge. (SEMI-CENTENARY printing: kept separate per owner's open merge question.)

events.name: Four days' meeting at Freehold, N.J.
events.location: In a grove near the A.M.E. church, Freehold, N.J.
events.description: A four-days' meeting (commencing August 23) will be held at Freehold, N.J., in a grove near the A.M.E. church. Revs. George E. Boyer and J. R. V. Morgan are expected to be present. All ministers and friends are invited. Wm. H. Turner [VERIFY], Min. in Charge. August 18-1t.

events.name: Camp meeting at William Tilden's [VERIFY] woods near Cookstown, N.J.
events.location: Woods near Cookstown, N.J.; stages from the depot at Bordentown, 3 P.M.
events.description: A camp-meeting (commencing on the 23d of August) will be held at William Tilden's [VERIFY] woods, near Cookstown, N.J. Stages leave depot at Bordentown, every afternoon at 3 o'clock. All friends of religion are invited. Refreshments may be had on the ground. Peter Gardiner, Elder in Charge. August 18-1t.

events.name: Special meeting at the church at Wilkesbarre, Pa., to raise funds
events.description: A special meeting will be held in the church at Wilkesbarre, Pa., for the purpose of raising funds for the benefit of the church. Bp. Wayman and Elder Schureman will be present. The meeting will take place on the 26th instant. Come every one. Wm. H. Chase, Min. in Charge. ('Elder Schureman' probably W. D. W. Schureman of the Philadelphia Conference: bare surname, not linked.)

events.name: St. John's Tabernacle No. 19, I. O. of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity -- grand dinner and festival
events.location: Grove of Mr. George W. Jones, near New Centreville, Chester Co., Pa. (Centreville station, Chester Valley R.R.; near Eagle station, Pennsylvania Central R.R.)
events.description: Notice. A Grand Display. Take Notice! that the members of St. John's Tabernacle, No. 19, of the I. O. of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity, will give a grand Dinner and Festival on Wednesday, the 19th of September, 1866, in the grove belonging to Mr. George W. Jones, near New Centreville, Chester Co., Penna. Tickets for dinner (lady and gentleman) $1; single ticket 50c. No officers named.
attendees: owner of the grove, near New Centreville, Chester Co.

events.name: Olive Cemetery lot owners -- election of Board of Managers
events.description: The lot owners in the Olive Cemetery are requested to meet at the Office, 921 Lombard St., on Monday evening, September 3d, 1866, at 7 1/2 o'clock, to elect a Board of Managers for the ensuing year. By order of Stephen Smith, Pres. U. B. Vidal [VERIFY initials], Sec. Aug 25-2t. (Notice reprinted Sep 1, 1866, which names U. B. Vidal as secretary.)

events.name: Harvest home at Gouldtown for the A.M.E. Church
events.description: There will be a grand harvest home in Gouldtown, on the 29th of August, for the benefit of the A.M.E. Church. There will be some very fine public speaking by Revs. James Lynch and Joseph H. Smith, and others. Come, friends, and spend a happy day with us. Joseph A. Nelson, Pastor.

events.name: Bush meeting near West Chester for the new A.M.E. church
events.location: Mr. W. Mettelie's [VERIFY] grove, near the borough of West Chester, Chester Co., Pa.
events.description: Notice. Bush Meeting. There will be a Bush Meeting held in Mr. W. [Mettelie's?] beautiful grove, near the borough of West Chester, Chester Co., Pa., commencing on Thursday, the 6th [VERIFY] of September, 1866, to continue over the Sabbath, for the benefit of the new A.M.E. church edifice now being erected at West Chester... No strong drink within two miles of the camping ground. Committee of Arrangements: Geo. L. Berry, Matthew Hogan, John Atkins, and several other gentlemen of ability. James V. Pierce, Pastor.

events.name: Camp meeting at Centreville (time table)
events.description: Camp Meeting at Centreville. The following Time Table is published for the information of persons desiring to attend the camp-meeting at Centreville. Edward Laws, Minister in Charge. Excursion tickets at greatly reduced fare, good from August 30th to September 6th, inclusive, from all points on the Philadelphia & Reading and Chester Valley Railroads, to Centreville. Passengers from Philadelphia take the 7.30 and 8.15 A.M. trains at Thirteenth and Callowhill, arriving at Centreville at 9.40; extra Sabbath trains on the Chester Valley Railroad from Bridgeport and Downingtown; on the Pennsylvania Railroad an extra train stopping at Penningtonville and Coatesville. August 25th-1t. (Camp opening date not printed; 1866-08-30 is the first day of the excursion tickets.)
attendees: minister in charge (printed 'Edward Laws'; LAWS-family identification not attempted)

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League -- annual meeting, evening session (continued report)
events.location: Pittsburgh [place per heading; read 'Pittsburg, August' -- day digits not certain]
events.description: Continued report. President Nesbit in the chair; prayer by Chaplain Nelson; the church choir sang. The committee to invite speakers reported that Col. John W. Forney and Hon. Mr. Bingham would address the meeting if possible. Report of the Executive Board read by Secretary White, received and adopted. Report of Solicitor Bustill on his year's labors read; amended to note that Rev. C. J. Carter of Harrisburg had sent the Solicitor a petition for Congress asking equality before the law. Rev. J. W. Loguen of New York addressed the audience (vote of thanks on motion of Geo. W. Sanders). STREETCARS: Mr. D. B. Bowser of Philadelphia, on behalf of the committee on Railroads (himself and Messrs. W. D. Forten and O. V. Catto), reported their efforts last winter with the Legislature to pass a law making it unlawful to exclude persons from passenger cars on account of color: the committee went to the Legislature twice and got the bill passed by the House, but, owing to the lateness of the session and the defection of a member who pretended to be its friend, it was not voted on in the Senate; he believed that at the next session, if started in time, they would succeed. Report adopted. Mr. Hughes of Harrisburg invited to address the League next evening. Mr. B. W. Arnett of Brownsville spoke on the League's work there and a joint-stock company and store. Mr. W. A. Bailey of Bucks County spoke for a National Banking Association; Rev. Jas. A. Nelson spoke of the colored men of Baltimore who purchased a ship-yard [value not rechecked]. Adjourned. Non-Philadelphia speakers in text only.

events.name: National Equal Rights League -- Executive Board protest against the Nashville call
events.description: Letter dated Philadelphia, Aug. 25th, 1866, from members of the Executive Board of the National Equal Rights League to President John M. Langston, objecting to his proclamation summoning the League to Nashville, Tennessee, and asking that the meeting be held at Washington, D.C. Cites a resolution of the Executive Board's quarterly meeting of June 20th, 1866, offered by Mr. Bassett, authorizing First Vice President Nesbit to confer. Signed William Nesbit, Altoona, Pa.; E. D. Bassett, Philadelphia; Sam'l G. Gold, New Jersey; and others.

events.name: Book Committee of the A.M.E. Book Concern -- appeal to ministers (roster)
events.description: Standing appeal (marked tf) of the Book Committee urging ministers and agents to remit money for books and papers; mentions improvements to the new property. Signed: Elisha Weaver, Ch'man; Stephen Smith; James Hollen; Theodore Gould; R. P. Gibbs; Wm. Watson; James Lynch, Secretary. May have begun in an earlier issue (tf).

events.name: Rev. Henry M. Turner arrives in Philadelphia from the Georgia mission
events.description: MIGRATION/SOUTHERN MISSION: Rev. Henry M. Turner, missionary in Georgia, arrived in Philadelphia on the 22d instant from Georgia; visiting his family at Washington; procuring Sabbath-school books; going on to New York. He spoke at the Bethel Sabbath School gathering (see p3). Also: Rev. Chas. Bradwell, missionary at Edisto Island, S.C., now in Washington (non-Phila).

events.name: Bethel Sabbath School gathering
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church, main audience room and basement, Philadelphia
events.description: Held 'Wednesday afternoon' (= Aug 29, 1866, computed from the Sep 1 issue). Singing and prayer by Rev. James Hollen; addresses by Rev. James Lynch, Editor of the Christian Recorder; Mr. Albert Griffin, Editor of the Nationalist (Mobile); Rev. Henry M. Turner, Missionary in Georgia; and Dr. Armstrong. Refreshments in the basement; superintendent and teachers credited but not named.

events.name: Semi-Centenary Camp Meeting near Eddington Station
events.description: SEMI-CENTENARY (record separately): 'The Semi-Centenary Camp Meeting near Eddington Station' under Rev. Thomas N. Kinnaird [VERIFY surname], Elder; last Sabbath the 26th instant more than 10,000 present; continues through the week and next Sabbath. Signed H. C.

events.name: United Order of Love and Charity -- Grand Excursion to Salem, N.J.
events.location: Steamer Portsmouth from the first wharf below Spruce street, Philadelphia (7 1/2 a.m.) and Federal street wharf, Camden (8 a.m.), to Salem, N.J.; stops at Chester and Newcastle, Del.
events.description: PARADES/EXCURSIONS: Grand Excursion by the Members of the United Order of Love and Charity. Delmonico Cornet Brass and String Band engaged, Mr. Jacob Boyer, leader, No. 1444 Apple street, Philadelphia. Tickets $1, to be had at the office of this paper and of the committee. Committee of Arrangements (addresses as printed, apparently Camden): Mr. and Mrs. Emery, Division St. [number uncertain]; Mrs. Gibson and E. Williams, 241 Spruce St.; H. Temple, 245 Division St.; Mr. A. B. White, Cherry St. [number uncertain]; G. Watson, rear of 210 Pine St.; H. H[i]nton [VERIFY], 227 Cherry St.; Annie Murray, Sycamore St.; J. E. Simpson, 239 Spruce St. Addresses in the A.M.E. Church at Salem by Revs. N. H. Turpin and G. E. Boyer, and an officer of the United Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity of N.J. [name uncertain]. Marked 3t.

events.name: T. G. Steward: transfer from the Philadelphia Conference to the South Carolina mission (account)
events.location: Bridgeton, N.J. (dateline); Beaufort, Summerville and Marion, S.C.
events.description: MIGRATIONS/SOUTHERN MISSION: T. G. Steward (dated Bridgeton, N.J., Aug. 1866) writes that in spring 1865 he was transferred from the Philadelphia Annual Conference to the South Carolina Mission Conference; worked at Beaufort and Summerville, S.C. (under Rev. R. H. Cain, Superintendent), taught a school at Marion, S.C. under the New England [Freedmen's] Society and organized an A.M.E. church there; in July met Rev. B. T. Tanner, pastor of Bethel, Baltimore; complains the S.C. Conference received only $309 from the society; is preparing to start back south.
attendees: author; missionary transferred from Philadelphia Conference

events.name: Southern Loyalists' Convention -- reception procession in Philadelphia
events.location: Chestnut Street to Independence Square, Union League House, National Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: PARADES (editorial account): on 'Monday morning last' (Sep 3, 1866) the Southern Loyalist delegates formed in line on Chestnut street and marched amidst applause to Independence Square, met by the Northern delegates and various civic and military organizations, then to the Union League House where Charles Gibbons, Esq., gave the address of welcome (Gov. Hamilton of Texas responded); convention organized at National Hall (Hon. James Speed president). Judge Hugh L. Bond of Baltimore offered a negro-suffrage resolution. Frederick Douglass walked in the procession arm in arm with Theodore Tilton of the New York Independent and addressed the New York delegation at the Union League House. No Philadelphia Black marchers or societies are named; white officials and Douglass in text only.

events.name: Centenary of American Methodism -- A.M.E. plan: first Sunday in October thanksgiving and collection
events.description: CENTENARY OF METHODISM (not the Semi-Centenary): editorial quoting paragraph 6 of the bishops' 'Plan of celebrating the Semi-Centenary of the African M. E. Church' (published last January): as the M.E. Church invited the whole Methodist family to join the Centenary of Methodism in America, the A.M.E. Church will celebrate it 'in our way, and in our churches, in October next'; every minister to set apart the first Sunday in October as a day of thanksgiving for the introduction of Methodism on this continent and lift a special collection, appropriated as are the Semi-Centenary collections. Date = first Sunday of October 1866 (computed). No Philadelphia committee named.

events.name: Miss Mary A. Still returns from the Beaufort, S.C. mission
events.location: Beaufort, S.C. to Philadelphia (residence of William Still)
events.description: MIGRATIONS/SOUTHERN MISSION: Miss Mary A. Still returned from Beaufort, S.C., after nearly two years as a missionary there; 'beloved by all of the people'; sister of William Still of Philadelphia, may be found at his residence. Same item: Rev. Stephen Smith returned from Cape May after nine weeks; Rev. Bro. Pearce, Elder of the A.M.E. Church in charge of the missions in Florida, is in the city.

events.name: Love and Charity -- Harvest Home at Woodbury, N.J.
events.location: Woodbury, N.J. (cars from Market Street wharf, Philadelphia)
events.description: Grand Harvest Home given by the members of Love and Charity for the benefit of their hall; eminent speakers expected; good brass band in the evening [reading]; cars from Market Street wharf. No officers named. Cf. the United Order of Love and Charity excursion to Salem (Sep 26).

events.name: A.M.E. Church, Burlington, N.J. -- public collection
events.description: Public collection to raise $500 for church relief; evening sermon by a minister from Philadelphia; Philadelphia clerical brethren invited to help. Jacob Mitchell, Pastor. (Day '9th' read; not rechecked at 1600.)

events.name: Harvest Home at Princeton, N.J.
events.description: Harvest Home on Wednesday the 22d ultimo (Aug 22, 1866) under the pastor Rev. Mr. Hamilton and committee (Princeton is a Philadelphia Conference station). Speakers: Rev. Mr. Seaton of Wilmington, Del.; Mrs. Frances E. W. Harper (writer compares her to Frederick Douglass); Rev. Mr. Goold of Philadelphia solicited the collection. Surname-only clergy text only (probably J. Hamilton and T. Gould of the Philadelphia Conference committee roster in this issue -- not asserted).

events.name: Suffrage meeting at Wesley Church, Lombard Street
events.location: Wesley Church, Lombard street, Philadelphia (Lombard Street Wesley = BIG WESLEY, A.M.E. Zion, per owner ruling)
events.description: EQUAL RIGHTS/SUFFRAGE: 'Monday night last' (= Sep 10, 1866). Mr. Wm. Nesbit in the chair; 'the Secretary' (unnamed) present; Mr. Nicholson [surname only], an officer in the Custom House, made a telling speech on Andrew Johnson and the political questions; Dr. Kent [surname only] spoke and later tried to read a preamble and resolutions; Mr. Joseph Bustill, chairman of a committee appointed at a previous meeting, objected and presented his report: a proposed test in the United States Supreme Court of the right of colored men to vote in Pennsylvania, and a request that the colored people of Penn[sylvania] authorize the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League to raise five thousand dollars for that purpose; report received, motion to adopt lost, Mr. Judah [surname only] alone voting in the affirmative. Mr. James R. Gordon followed; his preamble and resolutions were adopted: they recount disfranchisement by the Reform Convention of 1838 inserting the word 'white', the service of colored soldiers in 1812 and the late war, and resolve to petition the coming Legislature.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church -- communion Sabbath and evening sermon
events.description: 'Last Sabbath' (Sep 9, 1866): Lord's Supper administered in the afternoon, several itinerant ministers present; at night Rev. Elisha Weaver preached. Pastor Rev. R. P. Gibbs.

events.name: Bethel Church -- missionary collection
events.description: Rev. James Hollen, pastor of Bethel, proposes to take up a missionary collection on Sunday the 23d inst., hoping it will be the largest Old Bethel has ever given.

events.name: Political meeting at Bethel Church with Southern Loyalist delegates
events.description: Sunday evening last (Sep 9, 1866): Col. Stancel [surname uncertain] and Mr. Van Vliet, delegates to the Southern Loyalists' Convention (white Southern Unionists), introduced by Rev. James Hollen; described the situation of white Unionists and colored men in the South. Editorial remarks that a political meeting held 'in old Bethel Church, on a Sunday night' shows the colored people are aroused.

events.name: National Equal Rights League -- Nashville meeting revoked; called for Washington, D.C.
events.location: Bureau of the N.E.R. League, Philadelphia (dateline)
events.description: Notice from the Bureau of the National Equal Rights League, Philadelphia, Sept. 3d, 1866: owing to the removal of Brevet Major-General Clinton B. Fisk as Assistant Commissioner of the Freedmen's Bureau at Nashville, the Executive Board judges the meeting cannot safely be held at Nashville; it will instead be held at Washington, D.C., on the second Tuesday in January, at 10 o'clock a.m. Auxiliary associations and subordinate leagues invited; the League makes no distinction on account of color or sex. No officers' names printed. Follows the Sep 1 p1 Executive Board protest (Nesbit, Bassett, Gold).

events.name: Centenary of Methodism -- Philadelphia Conference committee appointed by Bishop Wayman
events.location: Philadelphia and New York Conferences (notice dated Baltimore, Sept. 10th, 1866)
events.description: CENTENARY OF METHODISM (distinct from the A.M.E. Semi-Centenary, though the notice cites the Philadelphia and New York Conferences' lead in last spring's Semi-Centenary collection). Bishop A. W. Wayman recommends setting apart the last Sunday of next month (October) for the Centenary collection; the central committee may make such arrangements as it thinks best. PHILADELPHIA CONFERENCE COMMITTEE as printed: James Hollen, W. M. Watson, G. [E. or K.] Boyer, R. P. Gibbs, Jas. Lynch, W. W. Grimes, William Moore, E. Weaver, [R.] P. S[ea]ton [VERIFY], J. Mitchel, R. Morr[?] [VERIFY], N. H. Turpin, J. Hamilton, J. Young, T. Gould and H. J. Rhodes. New York Conference committee (text only): D. Durrell, H. Davis, Joshua Woodlin, E. T. Thompson, W. H. Ross, J. M. Williams, Leonard Patterson and H. M. [Winder?]. Notice begins at the foot of p2 col7 and ends at the top of p3 col1.

events.name: Emancipation celebration at West Chester (4th anniversary of the Proclamation)
events.location: Chester County Agricultural Fair Grounds, West Chester, Pa.
events.description: PARADES/CELEBRATIONS: colored citizens of Chester and adjoining counties; general invitation to all societies and individuals -- Masons, Odd Fellows, civic and military; Rev. Henry Highland Garnett of Washington City chief orator, other distinguished speakers; the 'Boys in Blue' have promised to attend in large numbers; a splendid brass band engaged. By order of the Committee of Arrangements (no names printed).

events.name: 'Camp meeting in the church' at the A.M.E. Zion Mission Church
events.location: A.M.E. Zion Mission Church, 7th below Dickerson Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Extra (protracted) meeting from Sabbath Sept. 16 for a week or ten days. Order of exercises: prayer meeting 5-7 a.m.; 10 o'clock prayer meeting or preaching; preaching at 3 and 8 p.m. Rev. Wm. M. Watson to preach at 10:30, Rev. Elisha Weaver at 3 p.m. Theodore Gould, Minister in charge. NOTE: printed 'A. M. E. Zion Mission Church' although its preachers are A.M.E. (Gould, Watson, Weaver) -- recorded as printed; denomination question for owner.

events.name: Ladies' Aid Society of the A.M.E. Church, Chester, Pa. -- organized
events.description: Organized June 20 (1866) by the ladies of the A.M.E. church of the city of Chester for the benefit of the church and ministers; over $50 accumulated; forty members as of Sept. 5. Signed E. H. D. No officers named.

events.name: Chester Circuit quarterly meetings
events.description: Quarterly meetings of the Chester Circuit (Philadelphia Conference): Hor[?]town Sept. 29th and 30th, 1866 [place name blurred]; Chester Oct. 6th and 7th; Chichester Oct. 13th and 14th. Jeremiah Young, Minister. ('J. Young' is on the Centenary committee in this issue -- probably the same; not asserted.)

events.name: Home for Aged and Infirm Colored Persons -- appeal for a larger building (officers)
events.description: Appeal (begins p2 col7, continues p3 col1). The institution relieves worthy and industrious colored men and women in old age; inmates aged 70 to 104, of various sects, several Methodists; religious meetings on the Sabbath by ministers of different denominations. The Home is full; managers seek funds to purchase a more commodious building, which would also allow a department for aged colored men. Contributions to: Samuel R. Shipley, Treasurer, 111 South Fourth Street; Dillwyn Parrish, President, 1017 Cherry Street; Rev. Stephen Smith, Vice-Pres., 921 Lombard Street; M. Balderston, Secretary, 902 Spring Garden Street; Rev. Wm. J. Alston, Chairman Board of Managers, 632 Powell Street. (Shipley, Parrish and Balderston are white Quaker managers -- linked as institutional officers; owner may prefer text only.)

events.name: M. W. Grand Lodge of Pennsylvania (A.Y.M., South Seventh Street) -- three lodges established at Petersburg, Va.
events.location: Grand Lodge, South Seventh Street, Philadelphia (notice); lodges at Petersburg, Va.
events.description: SOCIETY/LODGE + MIGRATION of Philadelphia institutions southward: notice dated Philadelphia, September 10th [day digit read '10'], A.D. 1866 (A.L. 5866). Grand Master Brother Jonathan Miller has established three lodges in Petersburg, Va.: Treaty Lodge -- James H. Jones, W.M.; W. Jones, G.W. [sic]; Chas. Heath, J.W.; Virginia Lodge -- Joseph Robinson, W.M.; Richard Crosby, S.W.; Lewis Robinson, J.W.; Abraham Lodge -- Dennis Stokes, W.M.; Thaddeus Wedkins [?], G.W. [sic]; Edw. Stokes, J.W. Attest: Daniel Johnson, Grand Recording Secretary. Marked Sept 22--2t. Petersburg officers are non-Philadelphia (text only); the Philadelphia Grand Lodge officers are linked.

events.name: Burlington circuit quarterly meetings (Burlington, Mount Holly, Evesham, N.J.)
events.description: Quarterly Meeting Conference at Burlington, N.J., October 13th, 1866, 10 a.m.; Quarterly Meeting at Mount Holly, October 21st; at Evesham, October 28th. Jacob Mitchell, Pastor. Sept 22--2t.

events.name: Philadelphians in the South Carolina and Georgia missions (Cain and Turner letters)
events.location: Charleston and Sumter District, S.C.; Augusta and Macon, Ga.
events.description: MIGRATIONS/SOUTHERN MISSION: R. H. Cain (Charleston, Sept. 18) reports appointing Brother Wm. M. Johnson, 'formerly of Philadelphia', as a pastor in South Carolina [station read as Sumter District -- not certain]; T. G. Steward has arrived and has charge of the Morris Street church, Charleston (after his Sep 8 letter from Bridgeton, N.J.); A. L. Stanford (the Recorder's Philadelphia corresponding editor) is working in Georgia. Henry M. Turner's letter (Macon, Ga., Sept. 17) reports leaving Washington the 6th, passing Columbia, S.C. (Rev. William H. Brown of Baltimore had failed to come), Augusta (Stanford recently there), and a Liberia emigration meeting at Greensboro. Non-Phila names in text only.

events.name: Centenary of Methodism -- Philadelphia District plan and committee (second roster)
events.location: all A.M.E. stations and circuits of the Philadelphia District
events.description: CENTENARY OF METHODISM (not the Semi-Centenary, though the notice links 'April we celebrated the fiftieth year of the existence of our Church'). Plan: (1) from Tuesday, October 23d, religious meetings each night of the week (one evening may be a literary demonstration); (2) Sunday, October 28th: early prayer-meeting; 10 1/2 a.m. sermon, 'Rise and Progress of Methodism'; 3 p.m. sermon, 'Education'; 7 1/2 p.m. sermon, 'Triumphs of the Redeemer's Kingdom'; (3) closing centenary exercise, [Love] Feast [blotted], Monday evening, Oct. 29th; (4) special centenary collection on Sunday the 28th of October as a thank-offering, retained by the pastor and paid at the next Annual Conference for Missionary, Book Concern and Educational purposes. Committee as printed: James Hollen, W. M. Watson, G. [E. or R.] Boyer, R. P. Gibbs, W. W. Grimes, Wm. Moore, E. Weaver, T. Goold, J. Mitchell, R. Barney, N. H. Turpin, J. Hamilton, J. Young, H. J. Rhodes, D. P. Seaton; James Lynch, Secretary. Compare the Sep 15 Wayman roster: this printing clarifies 'R. Barney' (the blurred 'R. Morr?' of Sep 15) and adds/clarifies 'D. P. Seaton' (Sep 15 '[R.] P. S[ea]ton').

events.name: Richard Gleaves leaves Philadelphia for Beaufort, S.C.
events.description: MIGRATION: Mr. Richard Gleaves, 'one of our most valued citizens', will sail for Beaufort, S.C., in a few days to go into business there. Probably the R. H. Gleaves of the captured boarding-house ad (633 Pine) and later South Carolina politician -- identification NOT asserted; for owner.

events.name: Grand Fair for the Book Concern and Christian Recorder (Liberty Hall) -- committees
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's notice (Philadelphia, Sept. 21st, 1866): Fair by the Book Committee opens Thursday, November 1st, 1866, for two weeks; each pastor to form Sewing Circles of the ladies of his charge and send articles to Rev. Elisha Weaver, No. 631 Pine St. [Weaver's address prints 631, not the usual 619]. COMMITTEE ON FAIR FOR BOOK CONCERN AND CHRISTIAN RECORDER: Mrs. Maria Hallowell, President; Vice Presidents Mrs. Margaret Allen, Mrs. Sarah Davis, Mrs. Ann Hollingsworth, Miss Martha Sockum; Treasurer Louis K. Seymour; Secretary Wm. C. Benton [VERIFY]. COMMITTEES REPRESENTING CITY CHURCHES: Bethel -- Mrs. Mary Frisby [VERIFY], Mrs. Isabella Coatis [VERIFY]; Union -- Mr. Charles Simpson, Mrs. Elizabeth Jones, Mr. Albert H. Hall [VERIFY given name]; Wesley (A.M.E.) [= Little Wesley] -- Mrs. Amelia J. Briggs [VERIFY], Mr. William Mellis[?] [VERIFY]; Zion Mission -- Miss Jemima Jones, Mr. E. P. M[ai]n [VERIFY]. All authorized to receive donations (tf). Related: 'Great Union Fair' notices Sep 22 p2 and Sep 29 p2.

events.name: Grand Union Centenary Meeting at Hurst Street Wesley (Little Wesley)
events.location: A.M.E. Wesley church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia (= LITTLE WESLEY per owner ruling)
events.description: CENTENARY OF METHODISM + A.M.E. SEMI-CENTENARY both invoked ('the hundredth year of Methodism in America, and the fiftieth year of the existence of our Church') -- record separately, do not merge with either series without owner decision. All-day meeting Sunday Sept 30: prayer meeting 9 a.m.; preaching 10 1/2 a.m. by Rev. James Lynch; 3 p.m. by Rev. Joseph H. Smith; 8 p.m. by Rev. D. P. Seaton. William M. Watson, Pastor; W. D. F. Ryle [?], Sec'y. Sept 29--1t.

events.name: Equal Rights demonstration and oyster feast, Oak Street Baptist Church
events.location: Oak Street Baptist Church, West Philadelphia
events.description: EQUAL RIGHTS: speakers Revs. T. D. Miller, C. Leonard, F. T. Boas 'and a host of others', with music; grand oyster feast after, proceeds for repair of the church; admission 25 cents. Finance Committee: J. R. Cam[m]el [VERIFY], C. Underwood, F. A. Amos. Business Committee: Mrs. E. Black, E. Stephens, J. Allman, C. Preston, D. Pemberton, F. T. Boas, Pastor.

events.location: Masonic Hall, Eleventh St. below Pine, Philadelphia
events.description: Fair for the sale of useful and fancy articles, Monday Oct. 1st, 1866 through the week, for the completion of the building of Zion Baptist Church of 'Keighnsville' [Kaighnsville], N.J. Williams, 1019 Rodman St.; Mrs. Spencer, 309 Tro[u]t St.; Mrs. Boyd, 824 Shippen St.; Mrs. Lopeman, 1128 Shippen St.; Mrs. [C?]arroe [VERIFY], 1112 Rodman St.; Mrs. [B?]rown [VERIFY], 614 South Twelfth St.; Mrs. Brinn [VERIFY], 1312 New Bedford St.; Miss Thomas, 4 South Eighth St.; Miss Cooper, South Tenth St. Sept 29--1t.
